attributes.body_ja:
「きっかけ」は (A) が (B) の原因（げんいん）や動機（どうき）になることを表（あらわ）す名詞（めいし）です。漢字（かんじ）では「切（き）っ掛（か）け」と表記（ひょうき）されます。この表現（ひょうげん）は「(A) だから (B)」や「(A) を契機（けいき）に (B)」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

「きっかけ」には主（おも）に二（ふた）つの形（かたち）があります。「(A) をきっかけに (B)」と「(A) がきっかけで (B)」です。この表現（ひょうげん）は動詞（どうし）の過去形（かこけい）や名詞（めいし）のどちらかと一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われますが、動詞（どうし）の場合（ばあい）は「の」や「こと」などで名詞（めいし）化（か）されることがよくあります。

多（おお）くの場合（ばあい）、(A) には大（おお）きな変化（へんか）を引（ひ）き起（お）こしたり、新（あら）たな始（はじ）まりをもたらすような出来事（できごと）が入（はい）ります。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「きっかけ」は (A) と (B) の因果（いんが）関係（かんけい）が明（あき）らかであり、(B) の結果（けっか）が簡単（かんたん）に予想（よそう）される場合（ばあい）には使（つか）われません。

そのため「きっかけ」は、(A) が (B) を行（おこな）うための良（よ）い機会（きかい）であり、その際（さい）に何（なん）らかの選択（せんたく）や行動（こうどう）が伴（ともな）うことを示（しめ）していると考（かんが）えられます。
attributes.body:
きっかけ 'chance', or 切（き）っ掛（か）け in its kanji form is a noun in Japanese that expresses when the trigger of (A) led to (B). It is often translated simply as 'because of (A), (B)', 'with (A) as a trigger, (B)', or 'with the opportunity of (A), (B)'.

きっかけ primarily appears in two different forms. (A) をきっかけに (B), or (A) がきっかけで (B). This grammar pattern may be seen either with verbs in their past-tense form or nouns. However, in the case of appearing after verbs, it will often be preceded by の or some other nominalizing structure like こと.

In many cases, the trigger of (A) will have the effect of instigating a rather large change or new beginning.

Caution

きっかけ will not be used when the causal relationship between (A) and (B) is plainly obvious, due to what would be expected or easy to anticipate result.

Because of this, it can be thought that きっかけ is almost always referring to the opportunity of (B) appearing because of (A), with some external choice being made, or action being taken on that occasion.

attributes.description: Are きっかけに and 契機に interchangeable?

attributes.body: Both can describe one event influencing another, but with very different nuance. きっかけ refers to something that triggered or led to a change, as in 入院をきっかけにタバコをやめた (I gave up smoking on the occasion of my hospitalization). に伴って・に伴い is more formal, often expressing a broader causal relationship, as in 高齢化に伴い人口が激減した (The population rapidly declined along with the aging of the population).

attributes.body: Both indicate events that lead to change, but differ in register. を契機に is formal and often marks major turning points, as in 結婚を契機に転職した (Marriage became the occasion for changing jobs). きっかけ is casual and broad, used for any kind of trigger, as in 友達の紹介がきっかけで知り合った (We met thanks to a friend’s introduction).
